_comment: Benchmark targets. Each entry is one binary to measure.
writes a --stats JSON. Timings come from cudaEvent, so
they exclude process startup and PPM writing.
style 'legacy' : takes no arguments and prints a PPM to stdout. Only the
whole-process wall time can be measured, and the scene
and sample count are whatever it was compiled with, so
the matrix entries are ignored for that target.
To benchmark the serial branch properly rather than as 'legacy', give its
main.cpp the same five flags and a --stats writer; see bench/README.md.
Build both branches into separate directories so you can point at them at

_disabled_targets_examples.name: cuda-debug
_disabled_targets_examples.label: cuda-debug
_disabled_targets_examples._note: Debug CUDA builds use -G (device debug), which disables nearly all optimisation. Expect 10-30x slower. Worth measuring once so you never benchmark Debug by accident again.

_disabled_targets_examples.name: cuda-block16
_disabled_targets_examples.label: cuda 16x8
_disabled_targets_examples._note: Block-size sweep. 8x8=64 threads gives good 2D locality but low occupancy; try 16x8 and 8x4 too.
